selftext:

comments.author: MightyBig-Dev
comments.body: Amazing. Nice share. Future looks fun

comments.author: Infinitecontextlabs
comments.body: What a cool concept. And they say the algorithms can't be creative.

replies.author: GlitteringJob9248
replies.body: I think fable is very creative indeed.

replies.author: DHI_Dev
replies.body: It’s cool.  Idk if I’d call it creative as it appears to be a less complex clone of this https://youtu.be/Gh899Lp0Cco?is=Pb4JccZOfL3YdfjK game. But to be fair to Fable,  most game mechanics these days are just recreating the same gameplay loops in different ways.

replies.author: Infinitecontextlabs
replies.body:
To be a clone one would have to know about that game first, no? I suppose since it's on the internet it's possible that it made it into the models training data but that game doesn't seem to be very well known.

If it didn't make it into the training data and the model designed it without that existing knowledge, I think I'd consider it creative at that point.

If you had come up with this idea without the knowledge of Lux you would probably feel you were creative. Would then learning of Lux's existence cause you to feel less creative? Or would it simply be that individuals can have the same sorts of creative intuition based on what they know?

replies.author: DHI_Dev
replies.body:
It’s pretty well known that YouTube’s video has been scraped to hell and back by the various LLM providers. 

And yes,  I’d absolutely feel less creative if I made something and found out it’s already been done.

replies.author: Infinitecontextlabs
replies.body:
That's fair, I don't disagree with you. I would think that if it was a clone it would be much more of a clone than what the OP posted. 

I do find it interesting that a single instance of someone having the same idea would cause you to feel less creative. Would time be a factor for you? Comparing a time gap of 4 years to something like 1 month, do you think you'd feel less creative in both situations?

For me, I'd still feel creative regardless. I think for me it's prior knowledge of something that determines if it was creative or not. 100 people could have the same idea and build something from it and I would still consider all 100 of them creative assuming none of them knew about each other.

I guess I just feel that not being first doesn't automatically disqualify an individual from being creative.

replies.author: DHI_Dev
replies.body:
Yeah,  for me I think I would.

I also doubled back and did a quick search for 2D platformers that use a light source to manipulate shadow platforms…. There’s quite a few of them.  Some of them with over 50k views.  

I would agree that if we’re talking about people in general,  sure.  For me if items solely on people,  it’d be more creative than an LLM just spitting out its training data.

replies.author: karlmillsom
replies.body:
Yeah. This is pretty much a recipe for giving up immediately. Go find me 5 games in the last 5 years, say, that were completely original, in no way derivative of something that had been made before, even unknowingly. 

The one game that comes to my mind is “Baba is You”. I’m sure there are others. But truly, 99% of creativity is synthesis.

comments.author: daddywookie
comments.body:
This is a great example of the weakness of AI game dev. Look at the guys face. He is bored as fuck.

A good game designer could think of many ways to improve this experience. A lazy AI dev with no idea of game design would just think the game works so ship it.

I hope all of us using AI to develop games are also remembering to do our studying and understand what makes games fun and why we are trying to build experiences for our players. Otherwise, what is the point?

replies.author: GlitteringJob9248
replies.body: lol I was just tired because I didn’t sleep when fable launched 😅🫠🫠🫠🫠

replies.author: daddywookie
replies.body:
We’ve all been there, but I think that is also my point. When I get a game mechanic working I am usually hyped. I don’t want to get into weird stuff like talking about “the soul of game development” but I do think AI game dev takes out some of the humanity of it all. We’re meant to be creating art for humans to experience.

When I’ve used AI tools to make game concept prototypes it’s just all felt very empty.

replies.author: Shootzilla
replies.body: You seem to be applying your experience to everyone's experience. Just because when you create using AI tools it feels empty doesn't mean someone else using AI tools will also create something that feels empty.

replies.author: daddywookie
replies.body: Just more of a general comment about one shotting something like this. Who really made the game here? There’s a world of difference between AI created and AI assisted that is worth exploring as it will become very relevant in the future.

replies.author: Shootzilla
replies.body: Do you think this was just a one and done prompt, like there was no iteration or back and forth or refining?
